title: A simple hypoplastic constitutive model for sand

source.local_filename: Num Anal Meth Geomechanics - December 1994 - Wu - A simple hypoplastic constitutive model for sand.pdf

scope: Instantaneous Eq. (21) in unresolved source algebra coordinates only. No Atlas sign map, stress update, spin integration, calibration converter, admissibility rule or public executable model.
coordinate_policy: Symmetric tensors use Mandel order xx, yy, zz, sqrt(2)xy, sqrt(2)yz, sqrt(2)xz. Signs remain source algebra variables; do not assume Atlas compression-positive stretching.

requirements: Finite six-component symmetric tensors and four finite coefficients
All intermediate and output values finite
audit_domain.policy: Algebra-only conditions; not physical admissibility. No pressure floor, eigenvalue guard or density interpolation is inferred.

findings.observation: Prose assigns negative tensile stress and elongative strain/rates. Eq. (1) uses the symmetric velocity gradient with a positive sign; the triaxial compression recipe uses axial stretching -1 and confining stress +100 kPa. A common source-to-Atlas sign map cannot be inferred consistently from all these statements.

At initial Poisson ratio zero, row 2 of Eq. (25) requires c3=c2, as does Eq. (31). Printed Eqs. (27) and (28) instead give c3=-c2 when their common denominator and numerator are nonzero. No corrected expression is selected.
Printed arcsin((Rf+1)/(Rf-1)) has no real value for Rf>1. No reciprocal correction is silently applied.

integration_requirements: Objective Jaumann rate from Eq. (3), p.835: objective=ordinary+stress*spin-spin*stress. Ordinary rate equals this fragment only at zero spin.
Rate-independent ODE, with no plastic multiplier or explicit yield activation; six stress components are the minimal constitutive state of Eq. (21).
No explicit void-ratio evolution appears in Eq. (21). Table II density-specific coefficient sets must remain distinct calibrations.
Nonzero initial stress trace required by the printed denominator; stress-free start and physical admissibility remain unresolved.
The norm makes the rate generally nondifferentiable at zero stretching; zero rate itself is defined at nonzero stress trace.

Section 3.3.1, p.846 uses forward Euler and solves for the radial strain rate at each constant-confinement step. Atlas adaptive integration would be a project choice with refinement evidence required.
